lessons.title: Plants make their own food
lessons.objective: Explain that green plants make their own food rather than taking in ready-made food from the soil, using evidence from what plants need and where they grow.
must_establish: plants do not eat food the way animals do
plants need light to grow and stay healthy
a plant kept in the dark loses health and colour, showing it cannot grow without light
the soil supplies water and minerals, not the plant's food

lessons.title: The inputs plants need to make food
lessons.objective: Identify and explain the three inputs a plant uses to make its food — light, water and carbon dioxide — and state where each comes from.
must_establish: light energy is taken in by the leaves from sunlight
water is taken in by the roots from the soil and carried up the stem to the leaves
carbon dioxide is taken in from the air by the leaves
all three inputs must be present for the plant to make food

lessons.title: The leaf as the food-making site
lessons.objective: Explain why the leaf is the main site of food-making by linking leaf features to capturing light and taking in carbon dioxide.
must_establish: leaves are broad and flat to catch light
leaves are green and this colour is linked to trapping light energy
leaves have openings that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out
water arriving at the leaf is joined with carbon dioxide using light energy

lessons.title: What the plant makes: food and oxygen
lessons.objective: Describe the outputs of food-making — a sugar the plant uses as food and oxygen released into the air — and distinguish them from the inputs.
must_establish: the plant makes a sugar (glucose) that serves as its food
oxygen is given off during food-making
inputs (light, water, carbon dioxide) are different from outputs (sugar, oxygen)
the sugar made contains stored energy that came from light

lessons.title: Light, water and carbon dioxide make the food the plant needs to grow
lessons.objective: Explain, in a complete sequence, how a plant uses light, water and carbon dioxide to make the food it needs to grow and store energy for later use.
must_establish: the process name photosynthesis means 'making food with light'
water and carbon dioxide are combined using light energy to make sugar
oxygen is released as a by-product
the sugar is used by the plant for growth and may be stored
removing any one input (light, water or carbon dioxide) stops or slows food-making and so slows growth

lessons.title: Testing the inputs: predicting and explaining plant growth
lessons.objective: Use the photosynthesis model to predict and justify how a plant will grow when one input (light, water or carbon dioxide) is limited, and evaluate evidence from such tests.
must_establish: predicting growth outcomes when one input is missing or reduced
justifying predictions by referring to the plant's food-making
interpreting simple observations of plants kept with and without light, water or carbon dioxide
weighing whether the evidence supports the claim that plants make their own food
